cohort: 68 pregnancies complicated by vasa previa that delivered between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2012, from nine maternal fetal medicine practices and their associated hospitals
finding: This study confirms current recommendations for vasa previa management, including risk-based ultrasound screening, early hospitalization at 30-34 weeks gestation, antenatal corticosteroids at 30-32 weeks gestation, and elective delivery at 33-34 weeks gestation, which resulted in improved neonatal survival and reduced complications compared with earlier reports.
mod_finding: Of the 49 confirmed cases of vasa previa, 41 were delivered by planned cesarean delivery, and 8 required emergent cesarean delivery, all for vaginal bleeding.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at delivery: 34.7 weeks for planned cesarean, 34.6 weeks for emergent cesarean (range 32.4-36.0 weeks)
